prCiGreen.title: vendor engine a38cbb2 into the fill job

firstExecutionFoundNothing.what: Deployed the vendored-engine image (digest sha256:3a044c2c...) and ran --apply --twice for all six counties in one execution (factory-parcel-record-fill-dp8xd, runId 7a751a28-a795-4e38-9f25-9c7dce9175a5). All six counties reported ok:true and drift:zero-drift. The full byRailState breakdown for every county showed ONLY value/unaccounted kinds -- zero absent-verified cells anywhere, on any rail, in any county, including Williamson where the numbers were byte-identical to R1B's pre-R6B after-state (24,966/257,604 on the dollar rails, unchanged to the row).
firstExecutionFoundNothing.whyThisWasTheSignalToStop: A real engine change that produces zero observable effect on a run that reports full success is exactly the case ENFORCEMENT.md names: 'a convenient result is a reason to distrust the instrument, not a result.' Reported nothing changed rather than treating unanimous unaccounted-to-nothing as confirmation the emission simply had no candidates.

diagnosis.root_cause: CAD_ROWS_SQL selected every CAD scalar EXCEPT tax_year; tax_year appeared only in `ORDER BY prop_id, tax_year DESC` (used by DISTINCT ON to pick the latest row per prop_id). Every cad row object this job built therefore had cad.tax_year === undefined. cadNullVerified's own guard (`if (cad.tax_year == null) return null;`) treats undefined the same as null and refuses the emission -- correctly, by design, to avoid inventing a basis year. The result: the emission was reachable and correctly scoped (proven in PARCEL-R6-CADNULL's own tests) but its one required input was never supplied by this caller. A starved mechanism, per ENFORCEMENT.md's own vocabulary: 'it has a trigger and correct logic but its input is never supplied, so it runs and does nothing. Both report as success.'
diagnosis.confirmedBy: grep on the deployed source confirmed tax_year absent from the SELECT list; a new regression test asserts the SELECT-list text directly (not ORDER BY) as the falsifiable check.

pilot.fix: Added tax_year to CAD_ROWS_SQL's SELECT list. No other query needed the same fix (grepped every ORDER BY in the file; the other two are plain `ORDER BY prop_id` with no companion field).

secondExecutionConfirmed.what: Rebuilt and redeployed (digest sha256:32e05ca3...), re-ran the identical six-county --apply --twice execution (factory-parcel-record-fill-6nmkc, runId be6e8441-1ab9-4e49-910a-57a6f7b96e98). All six counties ok:true, drift:zero-drift. Every previously-unaccounted count in the first run's byRailState now shows absent-verified at the IDENTICAL magnitude (value counts unchanged to the row), confirming the fix converts exactly the intended class and nothing else moved.

gapLedgerCrossCheck.note: Section 9's sizing predates R1B and R6; it remains the correct target for the five non-Williamson counties (nothing else touched their CAD-null population between the ledger and this card) and is explicitly NOT the target for Williamson per the second addendum.
gapLedgerCrossCheck.conclusion: Every cross-checked figure matches the pre-recorded gap ledger sizing exactly. No unexplained deltas found for the five non-Williamson counties.

williamsonPostCrosswalkState.explanation: These three rails show absent-verified EXACTLY where R1B's after-state showed unaccounted (24,966), and value unchanged (257,604). This is the expected outcome per the second addendum: the crosswalk-matched residue (ambiguous or zero-match R-prefix accounts, ~24,966) has no crosswalk-supplied value, but IS a matched CAD row (via identity join on the R-prefix key itself) with a real tax_year, so the null on that matched row is now correctly certified absent-verified rather than left an unlooked gap.

livingYearPartialCoverage.note: These counts are lower on the absent-verified side and higher on value than the dollar rails because R1B's crosswalk already converted most of the matched population to real values; the remaining absent-verified count is the genuine subset where even the crosswalk-matched numeric row itself lacks living_area_sqft/year_built.

marketValueAndLegalDescription.note: Consistent with R1B: these fields were mostly already present on the R-prefix row's own data before any crosswalk; only the small residual null count is newly certified.

negativeControls.result: PASS -- the gap ledger's own 'livingAreaSqft zero' row is 0 across all six counties (no stored zeros exist in this rail at all in the current data), so the >0 carve-out was not exercisable this run, but the module code path (livingAreaIsZero, a separate branch from isCadNullNumber) is unchanged from R6's own tests, which do exercise it directly.
